proof:
The accepted symmetric-core theorem gives the exact integer fibers, area, depth at $Y$, and the normalized denominator with $C_\lambda$ bounded above and away from zero. The core's central reflection makes every nonvertical cap through $Y$ have mass $Q$. Each endpoint has a pure-base isolating cap of mass $1+2\lambda<Q$. At base one and any mark $X\ne c$, shift the through-$Y$ cap with continuous normal $X-c$ to pass through $(1,X)$. It loses a positive own slab because $c$ is interior, so the mark's depth is less than $Q$. This proves global uniqueness.

Each displayed cap passes through $Y$ and is proper on the middle fiber. The $J$-pair is complementary, and the $G$-pair is exchanged by reflection in $y$, giving equal coareas within each pair. Thus the indicated response coefficients balance and the normals span the continuous plane. The two $J$ halfspaces cover the ambient space. At a middle mark different from $c$, one of the four normals has strictly positive evaluation at $X-c$; the translated cap in that direction loses a positive own slab and witnesses strict depth loss. The pure-base isolators witness strict gaps at both other bases.

At positive rates only base zero contributes because the other fibers have $x\ge1/2$. There
$$
x=C_\lambda^{-1}e^{-R/\lambda}-\epsilon_\lambda,\qquad
\frac{|dx|}{x+\epsilon_\lambda}=\frac{dR}{\lambda}.
$$
This is the change of variables for the inverse law $|\nabla_x L_\lambda|\,dm/L_\lambda$, including the continuous gradient length. On compact rate intervals in $0<R\le T$, $x=o(\lambda)$ uniformly, so the slice length $2(x+\lambda)$ gives density tending to $2$ and all points tend to $w_*$. There is no atom at $T$ for the inverse law. The left exterior facet has length $2\lambda$ and constant positive logarithm $T/\lambda$, giving the exterior defect and its uniform rate density. The sloped sides have surface densities in $x$ bounded uniformly and $|\log(x+\epsilon_\lambda)|$ bounded by $|\log x|+\log 2$ for small $\lambda$; their positive-rate part shrinks to zero. The same integrable bound handles the proper nonparallel $G$ section near $x=0$, so it has no positive-rate section defect.

At base zero, the actual $G_\pm$ cuts are $\pm y\ge(4/5)\lambda$. On the slice interval $[-x-\lambda,x+\lambda]$, each captures proportion $(x+\lambda-(4/5)\lambda)/(2(x+\lambda))$, which tends to $1/10$. At the exterior facet this proportion is already $1/10$. These values are unaffected by allocation at the null crossing points. At base zero $J_+$ requires $x\ge1/2$ and $J_-$ requires $x\le1/2$; they respectively miss and capture the entire slice for small $\lambda$ at every fixed positive rate. Both $G$ normals and the $J_-$ normal are noninside; $J_+$ misses strictly. The capture weight is therefore $(19/20)(1/10)+1/40=3/25$ under either specified convention.

In the limit both $G$ halfspaces contain $w_*$ on the boundary and $J_-$ contains it strictly, giving closed weight $39/40$. The single spatial atom has closed halfspace depth one there. But $3/25<39/80$. In the actual rescaled coordinate $y/\lambda$, the slice tends to $[-1,1]$ and the limiting two $G$ cut thresholds are $4/5$ and $-4/5$, each oriented away from the slice centroid. This explains why the projected atom's closed incidence does not constrain the actual selections.

statement:
For $0<\lambda\le1/4$, let $A_\lambda=\{(x,y):0\le x\le1,\ |y|\le x+\lambda\}$, $c=(1,0)$, $D_\lambda=2c-A_\lambda$, and $B_\lambda=(A_\lambda+D_\lambda)/2$. Take the actual integer fibers $A_\lambda,B_\lambda,D_\lambda$ at bases $0,1,2$, with summed area $M=7/2+6\lambda$. The unique global deepest mark is $Y=(1,c)$ of raw depth $Q=M/2$. The four actual critical caps
$$
G_\pm=\{\pm y+(4/5)\lambda(z-1)\ge0\},\qquad
J_\pm=\{\pm(x-z/2-1/2)\ge0\}
$$
form a finite spanning critical cover, with proper own cuts. Give them cap-law weights $\theta=(19,19,1,1)/40$ in the order $G_+,G_-,J_+,J_-$; the associated response coefficients proportional to $\theta_H S_H$ positively balance their unit continuous normals, where $S_H$ is total proper section coarea.

For any fixed $T>0$, use $L_\lambda=C_\lambda(x+\epsilon_\lambda)$ normalized by volume-mean logarithm zero and $\min L_\lambda=e^{-T/\lambda}$. Write $e=e_x$, $w_*=(0,0,0)$, and $R=-\lambda\log L_\lambda$. The gradient-weighted inverse law at positive rates is $v_e(R)=2\delta_{w_*}$ on $0<R<T$, with exterior logarithmic surface defect $2T\delta_{(w_*,T)}$ at normal $-e$. The actual selected proportions there for the four caps are $(1/10,1/10,0,1)$, giving noninside capture $v_e^{\mathrm{noninside}}=(3/25)v_e$, where noninside counts normals other than positive multiples of $e$. The incidence-aware good capture that additionally includes strict positive-parallel incidences is the same. Yet the limiting closed noninside incidence weight at $w_*$ is $39/40$ and the limiting atom has ordinary closed depth one. In particular the purported lower bound $(39/80)v_e$ obtained by multiplying that incidence by $\Gamma_1=1/2$ fails.
title: Closed point incidence of a global critical cover does not bound actual rate capture
